clue.text: Talks about river, providing maps

indicators.note: the word talks goes around the river abbreviation, enclosing it

parts.note: talks means chats
R is the standard abbreviation for river on maps

explanation.surface: A guide talks about a river while handing out the maps for the trip.
explanation.definitionFit: Charts are navigational maps, especially of seas and waterways, so the words are synonyms.

clue.text: What sounds like rough plan of action

indicators.note: the clue openly asks for a word with the same pronunciation as the next word

parts.note: rough means coarse

explanation.surface: A riddle asking which word resembles a rough draft of a plan.
explanation.walkthrough: COARSE (rough) and the answer are pronounced the same in most accents.
explanation.definitionFit: A course of action is a chosen line of conduct, a plan for proceeding.

clue.text: A number show anger outside church in American port

indicators.note: the run of letters from the first words sits outside the church abbreviation, holding it

parts.note: to show anger is to rage

explanation.surface: Someone at a crowd scene outside a church in an American harbour town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'show anger' reads as one verb phrase but gives a single piece; 'outside' wraps the run of pieces around the church abbreviation, which sits after the N.
explanation.definitionFit: Anchorage is the largest city in Alaska and a seaport on Cook Inlet.

clue.text: Sailor losing heart, away getting fish

indicators.note: a word losing its heart drops its central letter

parts.note: a tar is an old word for a sailor
away, as in not at home, means out

explanation.surface: A sailor, dispirited, goes off to catch fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing heart' takes the middle A out of TAR, leaving TR.
explanation.definitionFit: The trout is a freshwater game fish of the salmon family.

clue.text: All getting excited in some short race

indicators.note: the shuffled letters are placed in the shortened word
short means the last letter is cut off
excited letters are agitated into a new order

explanation.surface: Everyone gets worked up during a brief sprint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'some short' looks like it qualifies the race, but it is the shortened container; 'getting excited' shuffles All, and 'in' places the result inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A slalom is a downhill ski race weaving between poles.

clue.text: Not strict? That is forbidden ultimately in period of austerity

indicators.note: the letters go inside the season named after them

parts.note: Lent is the Christian period of fasting and self-denial before Easter
IE is the abbreviation of id est, that is

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of forbidden

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether a fast in which only the end is forbidden counts as strict.
explanation.definitionFit: Lenient means mild or tolerant, the opposite of severe or strict.

clue.text: Fate of man with wicked wife

definitions.meaning: one's ... in life is one's fate or destiny
the biblical figure whose wife disobeyed and was turned into a pillar of salt

explanation.surface: The destiny of a man married to a bad woman.
explanation.walkthrough: In Genesis, Lot's wife looked back at Sodom against God's command and became a pillar of salt.
explanation.definitionFit: A lot is one's fortune or allotted portion in life; separately, Lot is Abraham's nephew in Genesis.

clue.text: New fashion, the latest from our collection

parts.note: a fashion is a mode

indicators.note: the latest, as in the final, letter of each of the following two words

explanation.surface: A designer touts a novel style, the newest from the house's collection.
explanation.definitionFit: Modern means up to date or recent, a synonym of new.

clue.text: One odd curtain out of place with clashing colours?

indicators.note: letters out of place are put into a different order

explanation.surface: A single mismatched curtain spoils a room whose colours already jar.
explanation.definitionFit: Clashing colours fail to match or work together, a playful example of things not harmonised.

clue.text: Faulty fence — it I'd replaced

indicators.note: replaced letters are set back in another arrangement

explanation.surface: A householder admits the broken fence was the one they put up.
explanation.definitionFit: Something deficient is lacking or inadequate, so defective.

clue.text: Type to keep quiet in game

indicators.note: the word for type holds, or keeps, the quiet letter

parts.note: a type is a sort
P is piano, the musical direction to play quietly

explanation.surface: An instruction for a certain kind of person to stay silent during a match.
explanation.definitionFit: A sport is a game or competitive physical activity.

clue.text: Poem about senior member who participates in cricket?

indicators.note: about here means turned round, so the poem's title is written backwards

parts.note: If is Kipling's famous poem
an elder is a senior member of a community or church

explanation.surface: A poem about an older club member who still turns out for cricket.
explanation.definitionFit: A fielder is one of the players on the bowling side who stops the ball, taking part in the game.

clue.text: One missed wandering around American city

indicators.note: letters wandering around move into a new order

explanation.surface: A lost traveller misses a stop and drifts round an American city.
explanation.definitionFit: Des Moines is the capital of Iowa, a city in the United States.

clue.text: Recommends lawyers

definitions.meaning: verb sense: publicly supports or urges
noun sense: barristers who plead in court, especially in Scotland

explanation.surface: Puts forward attorneys.
explanation.definitionFit: To advocate is to argue in favour of; advocates are also professional pleaders in court.

clue.text: Fierce girl enthralling any number

indicators.note: enthralling, in the sense of holding captive, means the girl's name encloses the number

parts.note: Violet is a girl's name
N stands for an unspecified number in maths

explanation.surface: A fiery young woman captivates crowds of admirers.
explanation.definitionFit: Violent and fierce both describe forceful, savage aggression.

clue.text: What's held by raja's perfect gemstone

indicators.note: the letters held by the following words sit inside them across the word gap

explanation.surface: A prince's flawless jewel.
explanation.definitionFit: Jasper is an opaque, often red, variety of quartz used as a gem.

clue.text: Argue concerning a member of the family

parts.note: re means about or concerning
a son is a family member

explanation.surface: A family dispute about one relative.
explanation.definitionFit: To reason with someone is to argue logically or persuade.

clue.text: Something flowery one man replanted to cover middle of bed

indicators.note: the rearranged letters cover the central letter, holding it inside
replanted means set in again in a new order, as a gardener would
the middle of bed is its central letter

explanation.surface: A lone gardener replants something in bloom to fill the centre of a flower bed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'replanted' makes ANMONE from ONE MAN; 'to cover' puts the E, from 'middle of bed', after its N.
explanation.definitionFit: The anemone is a flowering plant, so something that bears flowers.

clue.text: A learner, individual without any classmates?

parts.note: L is a learner, from the L-plate on a learner driver's car in Britain
one means a single individual

explanation.surface: A single pupil sits in class with nobody else.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone with no classmates is solitary, by themselves; the question mark flags the example.

clue.text: In the morning fellow is found in capital city

parts.note: AM, ante meridiem, means in the morning
a fellow is a man

explanation.surface: Early in the day, a chap turns up in a capital.
explanation.definitionFit: Amman is the capital of Jordan.

clue.text: Maybe tense people beset by its forebodings

parts.note: present is one example of a grammatical tense, hence maybe

indicators.note: beset by means surrounded, so the word its goes round the people

parts.note: men are people

explanation.surface: Nervous people sense trouble ahead, troubled by their own bad feelings.
explanation.definitionFit: Presentiments are vague feelings that something, usually bad, is about to happen.

clue.text: Tree found in Angel Meadow

indicators.note: the letters are found inside the following words, across the gap

explanation.surface: A tree growing in a meadow with a pretty name.
explanation.definitionFit: The elm is a tall deciduous tree.

clue.text: King to behave theatrically to get control

parts.note: R is Rex, Latin for king
to emote is to act with exaggerated feeling

explanation.surface: A monarch puts on a show to seize power.
explanation.definitionFit: A remote is the handheld control for a television or similar device.

clue.text: Harmony when worker's organisation accepts old Bob

indicators.note: the organisation accepts the coin, taking it inside

parts.note: a trade union is a workers' organisation
bob is British slang for a shilling, an old coin worth twelve pence, abbreviated s

explanation.surface: Peace returns when the trade union admits a veteran called Bob.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bob' looks like a name, but a bob was a shilling, a pre-1971 British coin abbreviated s.
explanation.definitionFit: Singing in unison means together on one note, so in agreement or harmony.
